I am, as of right now, the IT person for a small bakery (currently 2 desktops, a laptop, 3 printers, a switch, a VOIP modem, and a Modem/router combo for wifi, 2 IP security camera, and 3 landline phones operating off of aforementioned VOIP system), who is looking to upgrade their security system, move their order management in house (currently using an online service), and add a few more computers. I suggested that perhaps the easiest way to do all this was to go shove a rack into a corner for the new security system and other hardware, but this idea does not appeal to the owner. Instead, she wants to go all the way up to a small server room so that there is room for future expansion. She wants me to handle this. Problem is, I have virtually no server experience, at least on the hardware side of things. My budget (as of yet undecided) will be razor thin.

Here are the essentials I need/ want to fit in

Rack based system, prolly 2 shorter open racks

Patch Panel
small NAS
Sever for Security camera system (we are going to add more cameras as well as recording functionality), and storage for the same
Server for managing customer orders (basically would need have an excel spreadsheet running on it, that could be modified from multiple computers at the same time, which will be "fun" to figure out)
An unmanaged switch (already have, is not rackmount, was going to mount to side of one of the racks)

Additionally, I was thinking, for my own sanity, since the space for the server room is far from the office area, I should move all PCs into rackmount boxes and run thunderbolt or something for IO so that they can be managed centrally. We have the 2 boxes mentioned above, and want to add two more.

Those are the things that actually NEED to go into the room, so, how would I go about designing such a setup, and what else do I need. As of right now, my shopping list stands as such

Patch Panel
NAS 1 Security server
security storage (likely part of the security server)
Customer order server
Unmanaged switch (have)

Racks (obviously)
Portable AC unit
UPS, budget permitting
PDU
Cable management solution (in addition to the patch panel)
Assloads of Cat6 (Will likely get 1000ft, connectors, and crimpers)
A second Nas, to be placed on the other side of the building for backup
KVM setup that can be switched between devices
Fire suppression
A new PC for managing all this shit

Plus the existing 2 machines, that as I mentioned, will likely be moved into rackmount cases and put in the server room

so, what else do I need, and what should I keep in mind when setting all this up. Sorry for the vague post, we are still in very early planning stages, but I don't want to make any critical errors that will cause problems later. Hopefully this isn't too open ended for this sub...
Totally inexperienced, was asked to design a server room for a small business
You don't mention virtualisation. WHY DON"T YOU MENTION VIRTUALISATION??!??
Your servers. You could just create an esxi system. Google it. Makes backup, expansion and other server tasks a doodle.
Alternatively you could skip esxi and use KVM. Licensing is way cheaper.
You have one physical machine running multiple virtual machines, or virtual servers. Very handy for expansion and maintenance.

Sorry but it seems like your doing a lot of this stuff for the sake of it. A server room would need cooling and security, moving from desktops to rack mount will depend on distances etc, there are many considerations as people more knowledgeable than me have said.

I would suggest a hybrid. You could probably get away with a decent server just for the video, that is your data hog and you will need storage for that video that should be in a fireproof safe. Possibly just a NAS in there. As for the glorified spreadsheet, why not use Google docs? You won't have to worry about backup or how it is stored it can be edited by multiple people at once, seems like a cheap solution for that? Also that one decent server should run virtualisation look at Ubuntu server 14.04 then for each thing you wanted a box for you can just fire up a virtual box. I know I have only partially answered your questions but what you are suggesting sounds like a 50k solution for a 5k problem, but I may be missing something.

Server for managing customer orders (basically would need have an excel spreadsheet running on it, that could be modified from multiple computers at the same time, which will be "fun" to figure out)

Nope nope nope. Never have multiple users editing the same file on a network. You are only asking for trouble. If you aren't going to use the online service for orders you need to buy an ordering system which works with multiple users on a network. Besides, you need a full database app for future growth for your ordering system. If you continue using Excel you will only shoot yourself in the foot and limit what you can do with it.

Just because Access can hook into an Excel worksheet, does not mean Excel is a normalized database. For each order, you have a header portion (who is ordering it, total of the order, etc) and detail items (line items that contains the part number, name of part, price per part, qty ordered, total for line item).

Part of your job is protecting the owners from themselves. If you don't stop them, they could make seriously stupid decisions which might actually kill the whole business.

I guess I've been a drug addict for about a decade now; ever since I was a teenager every weekend was alcohol, cocaine, MDMA, weed, xanax, LSD, K, benzos, amphetamines: I'd go on but I think the point has been made, in the parlance of our times, my group of friends were the people who could find, whatever you may have needed.

For about 5 years though, I haven't really been into the party scene, certainly not the way that I was in college; don't misconstrue my words, I still take my share of drugs (and your share, and his share, you get the idea...) but they've been much more focused on whatever intellectual, moral and spiritual trip that I definitely believe (through my actions and as far as I can ascertain, my actual feelings) that I'm on; aided at times with psychedelics, my preference appropriately being LSD, which I guess is my long winded intro as to why I've chosen to post here.

When I was younger I used to party on LSD, I used to take a couple hundred µg, probably candy flip, blow some lines, take some ambien; take whatever came my way, really, wake up not remember much except that I generally had a good time. There was no introspection, there was no substantive change in world view beyond perhaps the slight natural uptick in empathy that tends to come from having shared even mild psychic experiences with others. It was a trip, it was a ball... but it was no trip.

In the last few years a number of this group that has been tighter than the pants on Will.i.am has been trying to cope with a lot; members of our group have committed suicide, family members have died, one of us was institutionalized after breaking mentally to an extent I hadn't even considered in my youthful exuberance, most of our SOs who were still around finally boarded the lifeboats; in short the lights came back up and the world hit us like a ton of bricks. We've gone through awful phases with dissociatives, major benzo/oxy/alcohol abuse, we've made decisions that make teenagers seem responsible and have been seemingly just trying to self-destruct without anyone wanting to press the button. At the same time, as people often do as they see their lives falling apart; our conversations have become darker, more nihilistic, less connected to the reality that we're feeling scorned by.

Continuing with our good decisions, in the last year or so, we have decided that despite the disaster areas that our minds have become, doctors heal thyselves, and have plunged (informed intellectually, but entirely unprepared) into psychedelics hard and have frequently (monthly, at a minimum) been melting on significantly higher doses than before, somewhere in the 900-1200 mcg a trip range. It doesn't seem necessary to say to anyone who would understand, but it hasn't gone well. The growing sense of nihilism, absurdity, anxiety, dread, loss, fear permeate our sessions from the get-go; if no-one has a meltdown these days it's considered a successful trip. I've seen friends, brothers, people who seemed mentally stable (relativity) to me hours before lose their connection to this plane of reality and months later have not returned, they're no longer the people who went in. When my dad used to tell me stories from his less reputable youth he would use the phrase "never come down," which I mostly hand-waved as anti-scientific D.A.R.E.-eque nonsense; once you understand, I guess you really don't want to; what I would give a lot to be able to have that conversation with him knowing what I know now...

Yet, we seem unable to stop; we've created our own delusional world that makes perfect sense to us, but ultimately has to be considered madness as no one could appreciate our thought paradigms who even entertains consensus reality, maybe we're those black swans who somehow figured it all out but statistically it seems more likely that we've lost it (whatever it was,) we somehow certain in our conviction that the answer isn't to back off and let our brains process the trauma (for lack of a better word,) that we've been putting them through and try to integrate it into the world we're forced to exist in, but rather to delve deeper into our madness until we either snap or find a way to integrate back into functional human beings.

I know I can never see the world the way that I used to, I don't think I'd want to. That being said, I'm so lost in my head; so without hope, direction, purpose, grounding and perhaps most important, my fucking identity, that I don't know if I can ever rebuild my mind. I don't know if I can ever convince myself of the importance of what is real ever again. I don't know if I can continue to move forward with my head down in a world that used to seem to have such clear dividing lines and now I can't even begin to know what to make of it.

I'm far from the only person that this is happened to, I hear and read about similar things all the time. If there's anyone out there who got out though, did you ever feel good again, did you ever find something meaningful that agrees with this world again, how did you do it?

tl;dr: My brain is a fried egg.
Anyone ever make it back out once they were really lost?
